source: ដំណាំទុរេន (Durian Cultivation), Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries, Department of Agricultural Extension, 2015, 31pp
text:
This official MAFF cultivation guide describes durian as a tree that needs a hot, humid tropical climate with consistent rainfall or irrigation, and is sensitive to both prolonged drought and waterlogging. Growers are advised to select a site with reliable access to water, either from a natural water source (stream, pond) or a constructed irrigation system, since durian's water demand is high and uneven during flowering and fruit development, and a shortfall at the wrong moment can cause flower or fruit drop.

Soil: durian grows best in deep, well-drained loam or sandy loam soil that still retains enough moisture to support the tree through short dry spells; heavy clay soil that stays waterlogged after rain is unsuitable unless drainage is substantially improved, because standing water at the root zone is the single biggest risk factor for Phytophthora-caused root and stem disease in durian, as described in the disease entries in this batch.
